title: E2ER pipeline
description: A research process as data: an ordered list of steps, plus teardown that runs however the run ended. Authored in TOML and validated as the parsed object, so the file stays readable and the contract stays checked. See docs/PIPELINES.md.

name.description: Filename stem and the identifier passed to `e2er run --pipeline`.

title.description: The template's name on the dashboard, such as "Empirical study".

methodologies.description: Methodologies this pipeline is appropriate for. Advisory; does not gate execution.

steps.description: Executed in order. An empty pipeline is a mistake, not a no-op.

finalize.description: Teardown actions, run regardless of how the run ended — completed, rejected, cancelled, circuit-broken, out of budget. Not steps: each swallows its own errors and none can halt the run, because their whole purpose is to leave the partial artifacts usable when something has already gone wrong.

skills.description: Skills this template adds to a specialist, as specialist = ["category/skill", ...]. Merged after the specialist's own skills (never instead of them) for runs of this template, and recorded in the study's description and dossier. Each must name a skill file e2er ships or has installed.

sidecars.description: Machine-readable files this template asks a specialist to write next to its main output, as specialist = ["file.json", ...]. Merged after the specialist's own sidecars; a check of the template reads them (e.g. event_design.json for the event_window check).

credit.description: Work this template is based on, draws from or cites: the creator, their role (e.g. conceptualization, method, related work), the relation (based_on, related_work, cites), the work's title and address, when it was published and read, and where it was found. e2er.org shows a `based_on` entry as "Based on" with the link; the creator is an external creator, not an e2er account. A credit says where an idea came from; it does not say the creator endorses the template.

kind.description: strategist: hand control to the strategist engine. specialists: dispatch a fixed set. gate: run a deterministic check. aggregate: dispatch reviewers and combine their verdicts. researcher: the run stops for the researcher, who can approve, edit the named files, give an instruction for the following steps, or send a step back. preregister: assembles the pre-registration from the design files, stops for the researcher, and freezes it on approval.

name.description: The stage name. Logged as phase_start/phase_end, shown in progress, and used as the resume key — so renaming one invalidates in-flight resumes.

run.description: Specialists to dispatch. Required for `specialists` and `aggregate`; meaningless for `gate` and `strategist`.

check.description: Which deterministic check to run. Required for `gate`. event_window verifies an event study's design (event_design.json) before estimation: estimation window length and gap, overlapping events, event dates in the data calendar. package_integrity, sandbox and reproduction run as steps of their own in the replication template (no `after`): package_integrity downloads the Zenodo record the question names and verifies every file against Zenodo's checksum (SHA-256 recorded); sandbox runs the plan's entry points in Docker (pinned image, --network none, read-only package, limits); reproduction re-reads every number of reproduction_report.json from the run's output files. package_integrity and sandbox block in every governance regime. field_retrieve, field_network, field_main_path, field_robustness and field_map run as steps of their own in the field-map template: retrieval of the boundaries from OpenAlex, the citation network with its completeness check, SPC main paths and key routes, the same on every alternative boundary, and the map with its exports. field_network can be shadowed by a governance regime; the other four block in every regime. numbers and citations may also run as steps of their own (the field-map template has no review step to run them in).

on_fail.description: halt stops the run; retry re-runs the preceding step once; shadow records the verdict without blocking. A pipeline may escalate a check beyond the floor but never below it.

modes.description: Run modes this step applies to. Absent means every mode — which is why omitting it on an iterative-only step silently changes single-pass behaviour.

resumable.description: Whether a completion marker lets the step be skipped on resume. false means it runs every time regardless, which is how the estimation gate stays unskippable.

files.description: researcher and preregister steps: workspace files the researcher sees and may edit (top-level names only).

after.description: researcher, preregister and gate steps: act inside the strategist's dispatch, right after these specialists have written their output, instead of at this position in the list. A gate with `after` also runs before any group that contains the econometrics specialist, so the estimation cannot pass it by.

settings.description: gate steps: parameters of the check. event_window takes min_estimation_days (default 120), min_gap_days (default 10) and max_overlap_share (0 to 1, default 0). package_integrity takes max_mb (default 1000). sandbox takes cpus (default 2), memory_gb (default 4), timeout_minutes per entry point (default 60) install_timeout_minutes (default 45) and snapshot (package-date, latest or YYYY-MM-DD; default package-date). reproduction takes minor_rel_tolerance (0 to 1, default 0.10). field_retrieve takes max_papers (default 5000; a boundary above it is refused before its pages are read) and max_requests (default 300). field_network takes max_isolated_share (0 to 1, default 0.5), max_missing_refs_share (0 to 1, default 0.4) and min_papers (default 100). field_main_path takes key_routes (default 10).

label.description: The step's name on the dashboard, such as "Design review".
